defect: D17 (KEEP) / sanctioned oddity "letter-delivery recipients are ignored"
title: Letter-delivery subscriptions are logged and dropped; a recipient without emailAddress1 is dropped; the template defaults

oracle.activityBoundary: every callActivity argument and return value crosses oracle/lib/boundary.js
oracle.determinismCheck: the case was run twice at clockPinIso and the two document arrays compared

edits: hearing: prosecutionCases[0].prosecutionCaseIdentifier.majorCreditorCode set to "CDE04" so all five subscriptions match TFL via matchProsecutor.
subscriptions: five copies of the real nowSubscriptions[0], each with a fresh identity and informantCode "CDE04".
[0] emailDelivery false, firstClassLetterDelivery true — the letter-only case.
[1] firstClassLetterDelivery true AND email delivery left on, emailTemplateName "tpl_named".
[3] emailTemplateName deleted, to show the ir_standard default.
[4] emailAddress1 padded with spaces, emailAddress2 added and padded, secondClassLetterDelivery true.

digests.convention: sha256 of the written file bytes — `sha256sum <file>` reproduces each value exactly

nodeEvidence.what: `if (subscription.forDistribution && subscription.emailDelivery && subscription.recipient)` — all three required. A letter-only subscription fails the emailDelivery test and produces no recipient.

firstClassLetterDelivery / secondClassLetterDelivery are handled by logging "Informant Register does not support ... letter delivery distribution" and nothing else. Note these run OUTSIDE the email branch, so a subscription can be both matched for email and logged for letter.
`if (recipient.emailAddress1 !== undefined) { recipients.push(recipient); }` — a matched, distributing, email-delivery subscription whose recipient has no emailAddress1 is dropped SILENTLY.
emailTemplateName defaults to the literal 'ir_standard' when the subscription does not name one.
both addresses are trimmed; emailAddress2 becomes undefined (key absent) when falsy rather than null.
when no recipient survived, the mapper returns undefined, so the outbound body has no `recipients` key at all.

assertion: Five subscriptions are supplied, all matching TFL on informantCode "CDE04", covering one rule each. Assert EXACTLY, on the TFL document's `recipients` array — length 3, in this order: [0] recipientName "email-plus-first-class-letter", emailTemplateName "tpl_named", NO emailAddress2 key; [1] recipientName "no-template-name", emailTemplateName exactly "ir_standard"; [2] recipientName "trimmed-and-second-address", emailAddress1 "trimmed-and-second-address@pinning.invalid" with NO leading or trailing whitespace, emailAddress2 "second@pinning.invalid". And assert ABSENT: "letter-only-no-email-delivery" (emailDelivery false) and "email-delivery-without-address" (recipient present, emailAddress1 missing). Five things are pinned at once and each must be its own assertion so a failure names itself. Two of them are traps. First: entry [0] carries firstClassLetterDelivery true AND email delivery, and is included — a Java port that treats letter delivery as "not our channel, skip the subscription" drops a recipient who should receive email. Second: "email-delivery-without-address" disappearing is the KEEP — D17 records email-only as the product behaviour — and a Java port that raises an error, or substitutes emailAddress2, or emits a recipient with a null address, changes who gets the register. Both are sanctioned oddities in design_rules.md and neither may change without a DEVIATIONS.md entry.
